modes.title: Routed
modes.description: Use shot_generation.md plus routed feature skills.

dimensions.title: Project Type
dimensions.prompt_template: Project Type is {value}. Treat this as a first-class routing constraint for shot planning: bias scene-type selection, shot scale rhythm, blocking density, reaction coverage, and lens language toward {value} instead of a generic fallback. Keep the original shot_generator output contract unchanged.

dimensions.title: Base Positioning
dimensions.prompt_template: Base Positioning is {value}. Let this positioning directly shape shot temperament, performance emphasis, glamour level, emotional pressure, spectacle weight, and how aggressively shots move between geography, action, reaction, and detail.

dimensions.title: Project Language
dimensions.prompt_template: Project Language is {value}. All dialogue payloads, subtitles, on-screen text, signage, message contents, language-switch events, and any other visible or audible language artifacts must follow {value}; if a quoted line or visible text appears in a shot field, it must already be rendered in the target project language rather than translated later.

dimensions.title: Region Culture
dimensions.prompt_template: Region/Culture context is {value}. Keep shot-visible architecture, dressing logic, blocking etiquette, street furniture, signage habits, object handling, and actor business culturally coherent with {value}; avoid drifting into a different life system or mixed-region visual language.

dimensions.title: Era Setting
dimensions.prompt_template: Era setting is {value}. Preserve period-appropriate shot-visible details across wardrobe logic, prop handling, set dressing, lighting motivation, signage systems, and body language. Do not let contemporary defaults leak into {value} unless the story explicitly calls for an anachronistic contrast.

dimensions.title: Expected Model Family
dimensions.prompt_template: Expected model family is {value}. Optimize phrasing, subject counts, motion complexity, and image/video fidelity wording for {value}. Prefer prompt structures that stay robust under this model family while preserving the original field contract and cinematic intent.

dimensions.title: Generation Workflow
dimensions.prompt_template: Generation workflow is {value}. In the confirmed-storyboard workflow, preserve the existing markdown column contract but put the usable prompt payload entirely in Video Content / Video Content (CN). Keep the other prompt cells empty unless the user explicitly asks for static image prompts; encode start state, key motion phases, and final landing state inside the video prompt so the next production step can run directly under a {value} pipeline.

dimensions.title: Continuity Priority
dimensions.prompt_template: Continuity priority is {value}. Weight identity carry-over, environment geography, object persistence, transient accessory continuity, lighting continuity, and start-to-end state closure according to this priority setting, even when a more flamboyant shot alternative is available. In the confirmed-storyboard video-prompt workflow, adjacent shots must pass continuity through the previous-shot Video Content ending and the next-shot Video Content opening; non-video prompt cells remain empty for format compatibility. Preserve blocking, facing direction, eyelines, object hold state, motion direction, transition logic, lighting anchors, and compositional center inside the video prompt unless a clearly described on-screen action causes the change. If any shot carries host-bound VFX, preserve VFX phase continuity across the cut inside Video Content: the next shot must inherit or explicitly evolve the prior shot's effect phase, intensity, spread direction, affected surfaces, and reactive secondary elements instead of silently resetting the effect state.

combo_rules.title: Live Action Emotional Drama / Chinese
combo_rules.prompt: When the project is live-action emotional drama in Chinese, favor grounded actor-readable blocking, restrained but expressive lens packages around 35mm-65mm for pressure shots, emotionally legible reaction coverage, and natural Chinese dialogue payloads. Keep glamour and performance detail high, but avoid fantasy-like over-design or needlessly ornamental motion language.

combo_rules.title: Live Action Suspense Thriller
combo_rules.prompt: When the project is live-action suspense/thriller, bias the sequence toward controlled information withholding, pressured negative space, tension-first reaction timing, selective POV or reverse-OTS reveals, and physically coherent threat geography. Keep every escalation readable; suspense should come from controlled disclosure, not random visual distortion.

combo_rules.title: Fantasy / Sci-Fi Stylized
combo_rules.prompt: When the project sits in a stylized fantasy or sci-fi lane, let shots retain bold silhouette design, larger motif clarity, and more assertive perspective language, but keep state closure and subject readability strict. Spectacle is allowed; subject count, motion chains, and environment continuity still need to stay production-usable.
